The minifigure on page 2 (head, helmet, visor, torso, legs) is not in the piece list, so it is not recorded and I did not count it as a step. If it counts as a sub-assembly step, every step number here goes up by 1.

Steps 1-3 build the 2x6 plate (p12) upside down. The round plates (p14, p15) and wheel holders (p18, p19) are added after it but sit below it in the finished model. A grid position plus a rule that supporters come from earlier steps cannot both hold here: in the finished frame p12 would rest on parts from later steps, and in the build frame the step 4+ plates would. So I kept p12 and everything built from step 4 on in the finished frame, and gave the four underside pieces position null with rests_on []. Their real connections to the underside of p12 are in other_joins. This is a deliberate exception, not an omission.

Step numbering: 1 plate, 2 round plates, 3 wheel holders, 4 end plates and side handles, 5 mudguards, 6 jumpers and grille, 7 slope and clip tile, 8 flag and antenna sub-assembly, 9 handlebars, 10 wheel and tyre sub-assembly (the wheels are fitted to the model in the last main step). Bracket height: the positions use 3 plates for the bracket (lego-22885), as the catalogue seems to do, so p3/p4, ring 1 and ring 2 are each 3 plates tall. With the shorter heights the brown plates p17/p18/p29 and the top plate p46 no longer sit on the brackets in the positions, so those rests_on entries were dropped. p46 rests only on the pink brick p23.

Booklet steps counted through the whole booklet: sheep body 1-9, head 10-16, head joined to body 17, tongue 18, leg sub-assemblies 19-20 (2x each), tail pin 21, tail plate 22, base 23-38, sheep placed on base is step 39 (adds no piece).

The booklet builds ONE model out of two sub-assemblies: the sheep (steps 1-22) and the base (steps 23-38). The last page presses the finished sheep onto the base. The four feet (p3, p4, p5, p6) then stand on and clutch the base pieces p69, p70, p1 and p2. I record that contact in the feet's rests_on, because it is a real clutch in the finished model and because without it the sheep and the base would be two disconnected groups. This is a real exception to the earlier-step rule. The feet are added at steps 19-20, but the base is only finished at step 38, so the contact is made at step 39.

The same exception applies to p11, p37 and p39. In the booklet the blue brick and the long slopes are placed first and overhang the area where a later base plate goes. The blue brick p11 is added before plate p34, and the slopes p37 and p39 before plate p35. The plates are pushed in underneath afterwards. Their footprints are really under those pieces, so I list the plates in rests_on.

p77 (envelope) is a loose item in the box that is not built into the model, so it is intentionally left as its own piece. It has step 0, no position and no joins. It is the only piece outside the connected model.
The sheep body is connected to the legs by pins, listed in other_joins. The head sits on p24 through p22.
p93 (cheese slope on the head) is placed at layer 23, directly on top of p100. I count p100 as one plate high.
p57 (inverted 2x2 slope) is shown overhanging the front of the body, so I give it no support below. I treated inverted slopes as having studs on top, since other pieces are built on them.
Pins, horns, eyes, the tail pin and the tail plate are attached sideways, so their position is null. The tongue clip p78 is clipped onto the handle of p74. The pink tile p54 sits on p78's stud.
Step numbers follow the printed step numbers 1-41; the step-26 sub-assembly (sub-steps 1-4) is counted as step 26.

Grid: x to the right across the 12-stud width, y towards the top of the face (16 studs, ears at high y), face-up display orientation. Layer 0 = the four boat-stud feet; the white base plates sit at layer 4 and the face is built on top (layers 5+). The back frame and stand hang underneath the base (layers 0-3).

Frame/stand and base: the frame is added after the face (flipped model, steps 22-29) and its studs clutch UP into the base's underside. In the final face-up positions the base plates therefore sit on top of the frame pieces and clutch them, so the base plates' rests_on lists the frame pieces (and p100 lists p101, p87 lists p98/p99, round bricks list their boat-plate feet) even though those pieces are added in later steps. This is a deliberate exception to 'earlier step only': the physical clutch really is base-bottom onto frame studs. The frame pieces themselves are also given in other_joins.
Smooth tiles (yellow 1x4/1x2/2x3, blue 2x4, white 1x4) have no studs; nothing rests on them; they are flush filler beside studded plates.
